description: FIND-S2-001's fix (iteration 1 -> iteration 2) correctly moved the failure-recording boundary from 1-5/6-9 to 1-6/7-9 in BOTH specs/behavioral-spec.md's REQ-307 Edge Cases/Acceptance Criteria AND specs/verification-architecture.md's PROP-307c row and new Gate entry (8b). However, contracts/sprint-2.md's CRIT-203 -- the THIRD artifact this manifest explicitly lists for review, and the actual weighted (0.15) pass/fail criterion that gates Phase-3 implementation scoring -- was never touched. It still reads verbatim: 'A failure injected at each of REQ-307's 9 canonical steps in turn is recorded correctly -- steps 1-5 (before an identity anchor exists) append a minimal {child_id, status:"failed", attempted_ms, error} row directly via ledger.js::appendChild, never via buildChildSpec; steps 6-9 use the existing buildChildSpec-based REQ-305 path' (contracts/sprint-2.md:47-50) -- the EXACT stale iteration-1 boundary FIND-S2-001 disproved (a step-6/REQ-204 failure means no agentId was recorded, so the anchor is still incomplete, meaning buildChildSpec would throw 'missing identity anchor' if invoked for that case, per REQ-206's own Edge Case; routing a step-6 failure through the 'steps 6-9' bucket this passThreshold describes would produce either an uncaught exception or no ledger row at all). This is not a new defect this iteration introduced -- it is FIND-S2-001's OWN recommendation left half-done: that finding's recommendation text explicitly said 'Re-verify the CRIT-203/PROP-307c integration test plan explicitly covers a step-6-failure fixture whose expected recording path is the minimal direct append, not buildChildSpec' -- PROP-307c was corrected, CRIT-203 was not. RESOLUTION-NOTES.md's own change log (sections for FIND-S2-001/002/003) lists edits ONLY to specs/behavioral-spec.md and specs/verification-architecture.md; contracts/sprint-2.md appears nowhere in it. The result: this sprint's own governing contract now directly contradicts its own governing spec on the single most safety-critical edge-case boundary in this sprint's scope (CRIT-203's passThreshold: 'FAIL if any step's failure produces no row, a wrongly-shaped row, or a row misread' -- a literal implementation of CRIT-203 as currently worded would itself cause that exact FAIL condition for a step-6 fixture, since it directs the implementer/Phase-3 adversary to route a step-6 failure through the now-proven-wrong buildChildSpec path).
